problem: Calling f_T the 'cut-off frequency' contradicts the very next sentence, which reserves the −3 dB point (the usual meaning of cut-off frequency) for f_p. A student can carry the wrong label into the exam.
fix: Say: 'Some syllabi call it the unity-gain frequency or unity-gain bandwidth. A few older texts say cut-off frequency for f_T, but keep f_p as the −3 dB cut-off of the open-loop curve.'

problem: The plotted curve is the asymptote A = 2×10⁶/f, so below the pole it exceeds the low-frequency gain: at 2 Hz it shows a gain of 10⁶, five times A₀ = 2×10⁵. The caption's 'at 10 Hz it is still at 2×10⁵, the low-frequency gain A₀' also conflicts with the formula in Section 1, which gives 0.707A₀ = 1.41×10⁵ at f = f_p.
fix: Start the frequency axis at 10 Hz (or clamp the curve at A₀ below the pole) and write the caption as: 'at low frequency the gain flattens at A₀ = 2×10⁵; at the pole 10 Hz it is 0.707A₀, and the 1/f fall takes it to 1 at 2 MHz'.
